title: Article 357 — Exercise of legislative powers under Proclamation issued under Article 356

content.overview: Article 357 provides that where a Proclamation under Article 356 declares that the powers of the State Legislature shall be exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament, Parliament may confer on the President the power of the State Legislature to make laws and authorise the President to delegate that power to specified authorities. Laws made in exercise of such power continue in force until altered, repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other authority after the Proclamation ceases, and authorisations and actions under the Proclamation are protected.
content.glance: Under Art 356 Proclamation: Parliament may confer State legislative power on the President (who may further delegate). Laws continue until changed by competent authority after Proclamation ends.
content.study:
Article 357 operationalises State legislative power during President’s Rule:
- Parliament may itself legislate for the State or confer the State Legislature’s power on the President.
- President may be authorised to delegate that power.
- Continuity of laws after the Proclamation ends until altered by a competent Legislature.

Examination: conferment on President; delegation; continuity of laws post-Proclamation.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Parliament may confer on the President the power of the State Legislature to make laws.
2. President may be authorised to delegate that power.
3. Laws made continue until altered/repealed/amended by competent authority after Proclamation ceases.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 357 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 357 provides that where by a Proclamation under Article 356 it has been declared that the powers of the Legislature of the State shall be exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament, it shall be competent for Parliament to confer on the President the power of the Legislature of the State to make laws, and to authorise the President to delegate the power so conferred. Laws made in exercise of such power continue in force until altered, repealed or amended by a competent Legislature or other authority after the Proclamation ceases to operate.

examTips: Parliament may vest State legislative power in President; laws continue after Proclamation.

keyTakeaways: Art 357: exercise of State legislative powers during President’s Rule.
